answer: Each new agent must store a 64 MB shale-seeded data file and answer a random-offset read challenge within 3 seconds, every epoch. Faking N identities needs N distinct copies, so 1,000 fakes hold 64 GB and pay about 1,000 times the disk and bandwidth, while an honest user stores one file once. Validators send the challenge through a public inlet and check 5% of agents per epoch; a wrong or late reply slashes 40 POA of a 100 POA bond. A fake cannot see past the horizon of unpredictable offsets, so it cannot precompute answers cheaply.
